explanation: Constantin Perskyi used television in a paper at the 1900 Paris World's Fair, decades before working sets. Robot comes from Karel Čapek's 1920 play R.U.R.

claims.text: The word 'television' was first used by Constantin Perskyi in a paper presented at the International Congress of Electricity, part of the 1900 Paris World's Fair.
The word 'robot' comes from Karel Čapek's play R.U.R., written in 1920.
Working television systems were first demonstrated in the 1920s, more than two decades after the word was coined.

writerNotes: Television feels newer than robot, so most players pick robot; counterintuitive is true. Twenty years apart, so no exact days are needed. Self-check (9.3): lint run clean; every claim listed with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where honest; datasets: no pinned dataset covers it; rival test: argued for robot, an old Czech word robota; but robot as a word for an artificial worker began with the 1920 play; volatility evergreen, no time words, nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026; regional: both words are used in English everywhere; style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words; myths: no match in myths.json; mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item; doubts: c1 is a first-use claim and needs a reference check; any earlier use found would only widen the margin
